title: OTP rate limit is keyed by IP and token, so attempts can be spread across IPs
expected_behavior: A bounded total number of OTP attempts per invitation.
actual_behavior: 5 attempts per minute per source IP, unbounded across IPs.
root_cause: Limiter key includes the client IP only.
exploitation_scenario: Attacker holding a leaked link rotates IPs to guess the 6-digit OTP, then submits in the invitee's place; admin review still applies.
impact: Invitation hijack before the real invitee uses it.
remediation: Add a second limiter keyed by token alone (e.g. 20/hour) or revoke after N failures.

title: Session ID not regenerated after successful OTP verification
description: Verified state is written into the existing session without regenerate().
expected_behavior: Privilege change rotates the session ID.
exploitation_scenario: Requires planting a session cookie on the victim first (session fixation).
impact: Attacker could submit the form using the victim's verification.

title: Review emails sent inside the DB transaction
description: TicketIssued / InvitationRequestRejected are sent before the transaction commits.
actual_behavior: A commit failure after sending leaves a QR for a non-existent ticket.
impact: Guest turned away at the door with a valid-looking QR.

title: OTPs stored in plaintext and visible to every admin
description: Intentional per spec (admin must view the OTP anytime).
actual_behavior: Anyone with DB/admin access can redeem open invitations.
impact: Low given 7-day expiry and admin review.
remediation: Optionally hide the OTP once used/expired.

title: Any admin user can generate invitations and approve free tickets
description: Inherited from the project-wide lack of roles (root SEC-02).
evidence: routes/web.php admin group uses auth only
expected_behavior: Ticket-issuing actions restricted to authorised staff.
actual_behavior: Every user (including check-in staff) can issue free tickets.
exploitation_scenario: A check-in staff account issues itself/others free tickets.
remediation: Introduce an admin/check-in role split (see root SEC-02).
